new_findings.a_fourth_shape_n1: The criterion that failed unit 1 asks for 'a single sentence with NO SUBORDINATE CLAUSES' and pillars that are 'INDEPENDENTLY DEFENSIBLE'. A draft that HAS no subordinate clauses does not contain the words 'subordinate clauses'; a pillar that IS defensible does not say 'defensible'. This is prohibition-in-meaning with no quoted token list, so the fail-safe rule classifies it `presence` — correctly by the ruling as written — and it fails there. A PROPERTY-OF-THE-PROSE criterion: satisfied by how the text reads, not by what it contains. Unlike -010's equivalent finding, IT IS IN A COMMITTED TRACE. Exhibited once; unit 2's failing criterion does not obviously belong to the class, so it is recorded as an observation and not yet a design input.
new_findings.B16_MEASURED_RATHER_THAN_ARGUED: The same criterion, conceptually, scored 0.63 and PASSED in -010 and 0.43 and FAILED today. -010: 'a core promise of exactly one sentence with no subordinate clauses, and two to four supporting pillars that are each defensible without reference to another pillar'. Today: 'a core promise expressed as a single sentence with no subordinate clauses, and each supporting pillar is independently defensible'. NOTHING ABOUT THE CHECK CHANGED. A rewording moved a criterion across the threshold and decided the run.
